title: Virtue and vice
note: Amoral is not immoral: the immoral person breaks moral rules, while the amoral person does not recognize them at all. Probity and rectitude name settled honesty and uprightness; turpitude and iniquity name its opposite. A misanthrope dislikes humankind; an altruist puts others first.

items.a: strict honesty and integrity
items.ex: Her probity was so well known that both parties asked her to count the votes.

items.a: morally correct behavior or thinking
items.ex: The old judge was admired for his rectitude more than his brilliance.

items.a: careful to avoid doing anything wrong
items.ex: A scrupulous cashier, he returned the extra twenty the customer had left.

items.a: a feeling of guilt that prevents or follows wrongdoing
items.ex: She cut the line without the slightest compunction.

items.a: wickedness; deep moral baseness
items.ex: Some professional licenses can be revoked for crimes of moral turpitude.

items.a: gross injustice or wickedness
items.ex: The preacher thundered against the iniquity of the slave trade.

items.a: wicked or criminal, of an activity or plan
items.ex: The hackers' nefarious scheme targeted hospital records.

items.a: shockingly evil
items.ex: The court called the arson a heinous crime against a sleeping family.

items.a: deserving strong condemnation
items.ex: Mocking the injured player was reprehensible, and the league said so.

items.a: dishonorable and base in character or purpose
items.ex: He won the seat by the ignoble trick of spreading rumors about her family.

items.a: indulging in vice without restraint
items.ex: The dissolute heir spent his inheritance on cards and champagne.

items.a: sexually unrestrained; disregarding moral rules
items.ex: Censors condemned the play as licentious and closed it after a week.

items.a: an unprincipled, immoral person
d: a person who lives in self-denial
items.ex: The old reprobate cheated at cards even with his grandchildren.

items.a: a person who behaves badly or breaks the law
d: a person who gives to charity
items.ex: Some miscreant had glued the classroom door shut.

items.a: impossible to correct or reform
items.ex: An incorrigible flirt, he winked at the officer writing his ticket.

items.a: making a show of being morally superior
items.ex: His sanctimonious lecture on thrift came from a man with three boats.

items.a: clever but unsound reasoning, especially about morals
items.ex: By a feat of casuistry, he argued that breaking the promise honored its spirit.

items.a: lacking any sense of right and wrong
items.ex: The novel's amoral hero never asks whether what he does is wrong.

items.a: unselfish concern for the welfare of others
items.ex: Donating a kidney to a stranger is altruism of a rare kind.

items.a: doing or producing good; generous in giving
items.ex: A beneficent donor paid off the school's lunch debt.

items.a: a person who dislikes humankind
d: a person who denies himself pleasure
a person who reasons about morals
items.ex: The village misanthrope posted a sign that read "Go Away" in four languages.

items.a: wishing harm to others
items.ex: The villain's malevolent grin told us the bridge would not hold.

items.a: harmful, especially in a gradual or subtle way
items.ex: The pernicious rumor slowly drove customers from the shop.

items.a: spreading harm gradually and stealthily
items.ex: Mold is insidious; by the time you see it, the wall is ruined.

items.a: a model of excellence or of a particular quality
items.ex: The manual held up the old foreman as a paragon of safety.

items.a: serving as a desirable model; excellent
items.ex: Her exemplary record earned her the first promotion in the department.

items.a: to atone for guilt or wrongdoing
items.ex: He tried to expiate his years of neglect by caring for his father.

items.a: moderate in eating and drinking
items.ex: The abstemious host drank water while his guests finished the wine.

items.a: practicing strict self-denial
items.ex: The ascetic monk owned a blanket, a bowl and a book.

items.a: lacking reverence, especially for God or religion
items.ex: Villagers thought it impious to hold a market on the feast day.
